issue.title: Integer-tuple array comparisons retain extra chaining state for `!(a > b)`
issue.body:
I tried this code:

godbolt:https://godbolt.org/z/vxnGqf87K

```rust
#[no_mangle]
#[inline(never)]
pub fn direct(a: &[(i16, u16); 2], b: &[(i16, u16); 2]) -> bool {
    a <= b
}

#[no_mangle]
#[inline(never)]
pub fn negated(a: &[(i16, u16); 2], b: &[(i16, u16); 2]) -> bool {
    !(a > b)
}

#[no_mangle]
#[inline(never)]
pub fn manual(a: &[(i16, u16); 2], b: &[(i16, u16); 2]) -> bool {
    for index in 0..2 {
        if a[index].0 != b[index].0 {
            return a[index].0 < b[index].0;
        }
        if a[index].1 != b[index].1 {
            return a[index].1 < b[index].1;
        }
    }
    true
}
```



I expected to see this happen: for these concrete integer types, the two
predicates describe the same total lexicographic order. The result should be
computable with boolean comparisons, without retaining a separate "equal"
result encoding on a path where a difference has already been found.

Instead, this happened:

| Configuration | direct | negated | manual |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| O2 | 66 bytes | 73 bytes | 66 bytes |
| O3 | 113 bytes | 123 bytes | 66 bytes |
| Os | 44 bytes | 48 bytes | 44 bytes |
| Oz | 23 bytes | 23 bytes | 45 bytes |
| O3, `-Cllvm-args=-vectorize-slp=false` | 113 bytes | 123 bytes | 66 bytes |

The optimized O3 IR for `negated` includes a result-encoding sequence of this
shape (SSA names abbreviated):

```llvm
%signed_gt = icmp sgt i16 %a_signed, %b_signed
%signed_result = zext i1 %signed_gt to i8
%unsigned_gt = icmp ugt i16 %a_unsigned, %b_unsigned
%unsigned_result = zext i1 %unsigned_gt to i8
%inner = select i1 %unsigned_eq, i8 2, i8 %unsigned_result
%result = select i1 %signed_eq, i8 %inner, i8 %signed_result
%not_greater = icmp ne i8 %result, 1
```

This becomes conditional moves, an immediate `2`, and a final compare/setne
in the assembly. The boolean `direct` form does not keep this i8 encoding.
Disabling SLP does not remove the difference. The `manual` control shows one
compact implementation at O3.



### Meta


```text
rustc 1.101.0-nightly (21b707e3f 2026-09-30)
binary: rustc
commit-hash: 21b707e3f97e0b522ebd2f277a862339625ad83f
commit-date: 2026-09-30
host: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
release: 1.101.0-nightly
LLVM version: 23.1.1
```

nodes.body:
The generated assembly for the `direct` and `negated` functions may be larger, but also has only half as many branches. Can you verify that the `manual` implementation is actually faster?

@rustbot label -C-bug C-optimization

For these fixed-input microbenchmarks, each item performs 50,000,000 non-inlined calls. Times below are the median of three native wall-clock runs.

| Fixed input | direct | negated | manual |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| All elements equal | 120.620 ms | 140.159 ms | 108.839 ms |
| First signed field is less | 123.685 ms | 133.825 ms | 93.615 ms |
| Last unsigned field is greater | 157.667 ms | 165.570 ms | 111.782 ms |

Environment: AMD EPYC 7K62 48-Core Processor (guest-reported CPU model), 2 vCPUs, approximately 7.5 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, KVM VM, pinned to vCPU 1;

Compiler: `rustc 1.101.0-nightly (21b707e3f 2026-09-30)`, LLVM 23.1.1, O3, codegen-units=1, LTO disabled.

Thanks for the quick reply! I closed it by accident; the performance concern still stands, so I reopened it. The microbenchmark numbers are above, and I’m happy to share the harness/assembly or test a patch if useful.
